summary: A window render refuses by name on any git failure, not only an unresolvable cursor — touchedPast's fail-open already promises that bound
acceptance: Every git failure inside a window render reaches the woken slice as the named refusal; nothing escapes promptArgs into an uncaught tick.
tests: a window render refuses by name when git fails for a reason other than an unresolvable cursor
notes: touchedPast (harness/windows.ts:783) wakes the slice on any git failure and names refusal as its bound; refusal is reached only from the !resolves leg of renderSpecWindow:391 and renderSweepWindow:497. A throw out of commitsPast/diffOf/retiredLines/bootstrap escapes phase.promptArgs — uncaught at src/Dispatcher.ts:1957 and :3281 — so the tick dies with no verdict. Carry the failure's own text into the refusal.

summary: `runner` is declared `(api) => Runner` and called at chain load, so the vitest factory takes the engine's installer and the state root's worktree base from the API
acceptance: The declaration schema refuses a runner that is not a factory, naming the field; the chain factory calls the declared factory with its own FlumeApi; the vitest factory's base checkout is provisioned by that API's installer under the state root's worktree base, and no consumer constructs either by hand.

notes: Ruled in spec at 1d81a77. Breaking declaration-schema change with a chain-side twin: this repo's .flume/declaration.ts:63 still passes a vitestRunner({lanes}) value and .flume/ is outside build's fence, so chain load refuses every tick between this commit and the operator's edit -- an interactive session moves it the moment this lands. The package reaches the base as worktreesBase(api.paths.flumeDir) via ../src/paths.js; putting it on FlumeApi stays the parked question's call.
